title: Widen trial division's fast path to 64-bit bounds
description: Trial division's fast path (trial division factorization of_«,⁇from_»?«,⁇to_»?, Late Math.avail) was specialized to search bounds below 2^31 - 60, from when L2 had only 32-bit integer registers. L2 now has 64-bit registers, so widen the bounds to 2^63 - 60, letting the loop index stay unboxed for every number below about 2^126. Add a test that factors a product in [2^62..2^63 - 60), whose square root needs the widened path.

title: L2: compute masked and modular products without big integers
description:
Goal: let the L2 optimizer compute modular products in machine words, so Avail code gets fast modular arithmetic just by writing the natural expression, without asking for it.

1. Masked products. When L2 sees ((a × b) bit∧ m), where m = 2^k − 1 for some k ≤ 64 and a and b are known integers (not necessarily small), substitute ((a bit∧ m) × (b bit∧ m)) bit∧ m, where the multiply is the low-limb (wrapping) 64-bit multiply. The low k bits of a product depend only on the low k bits of its factors, so the result is exact, and no big integer is created however large a, b, or their true product is. The same holds for the masked operands of + and −, and chains of them under one mask.

2. Remainders of products. When L2 sees ((a × b) mod n), with 0 < n ≤ 2^63 and a and b known to lie in [0..n) (or reducible into it), compute the product's remainder without big-integer arithmetic: form the 128-bit product (Math.multiplyHigh and the low 64-bit multiply; Math.unsignedMultiplyHigh for unsigned operands), then reduce it modulo n. The JVM has no 128-by-64 division, so the reduction needs its own routine (for example a two-step long division on 64-bit halves, or a precomputed reciprocal per modulus when n is loop-invariant).

Motivation: the library's primality code (Late Math.avail) spends its time in modular exponentiation. "_^_mod_" and "_is a strong probable prime to base_" square values below the modulus and reduce them. For moduli up to 2^64, those products need up to 128 bits and currently become big integers. Sinclair's 7-base Miller-Rabin test for [2^32..2^64] does about 7 × 64 such squarings per call, which dominates the "primality tests" test. FJ32_256's hash ((h >> 16) bit⊕ h) × 0x45d9f3b followed by a mask is the masked-product case.

Notes:
- Both rewrites apply only when the operands' static types (restrictions) prove the preconditions: integer operands, and for the remainder, a positive modulus no larger than 2^63 and operands within [0..n).
- The results must be exactly what the unfused Avail operations would compute; this is a strength reduction, not an approximation.
- Avail tests should compare the fused results against the generic path on values chosen around the boundaries (k = 63 and 64; moduli near 2^32, 2^62, and 2^63; operands of n − 1).

title: Stop the I/O tests from flushing the whole drive
description:
Problem: the I/O tests spend most of each test run waiting on whole-drive flushes. Closing a file writer synchronizes it (Close_ on a file writer calls Synchronize_, in File Iterators.avail), and synchronizing reaches P_FileSync, whose FileChannel.force is fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) on macOS: a flush of the drive's entire write cache, about 16-20 ms each, serialized across the drive. While one is in flight, every metadata-changing call on the volume (create, chmod, unlink, rename) waits for it.

Evidence:
- A standalone benchmark on the repository's volume: create, chmod, and unlink took about 0.02-0.08 ms alone, about the same beside concurrent fsync, and about 20.8 ms each beside concurrent F_FULLFSYNC.
- The workbench's primitive statistics: P_FileOpen averaged 19 ms and P_FileSetPermissions 9 ms, while read-only P_FileMetadata averaged 0.77 ms.
- A traced warm pass: tests other than the I/O tests finished by about 134 ms, while the I/O suite ran until about 405 ms. Groups of I/O tests finished at the same instant (for example four at 118.4 ms, three at 248.296 ms), consistent with flushes completing together. Pass times varied from about 400 to 1,000 ms.

Sources of flushes in the tests:
- The I/O suite's setup ("Before running I/O test suite" in File Test Utilities.avail) closes two writers (abracadabra.txt, scratch.txt), gating every I/O test behind about 54 ms of flushing.
- "a private copy of abracadabra.txt" writes each copy through a file writer, so each of the dozen access-rights tests that uses one pays a full flush. These private copies exist so that those tests can run concurrently without interfering.
- Four tests synchronize deliberately: file iterator (refresh/synchronize), (alignment), (scattered write), and file(round trip) (the last is inside a block comment in IO Tests.avail and does not run).

Options:
1. In the tests: create the private copies and the setup's files without a file writer (for example with the library's file copy, or by opening and closing a channel without a writer), so they never synchronize. Only the tests that test synchronization would still flush.
2. In the library: stop Close_ on a file writer from synchronizing, leaving durability to an explicit Synchronize_. This changes a documented behavior, and callers relying on close-means-durable would need an explicit Synchronize_.
3. The FFM file layer (avail-rlc) offers cheaper sync levels (drive vs. durable), which removes most of the cost at its source.

Related: avail-rlc (FFM file operations and sync levels), avail-6s8 (file primitives no longer block interpreter threads while they wait).

title: Make the avail test task depend on the Avail module sources
description:
Problem: the avail project's test task does not declare the Avail module sources as inputs, so Gradle treats it as up to date after an Avail-only change and reports the previous run's results. A change that edits or deletes .avail files can show "BUILD SUCCESSFUL" from ./gradlew build without any Avail test having run against it.

Observed: after deleting a library module (Rational Number.avail), ./gradlew build finished in 2 s with the earlier test results; ./gradlew test --rerun was needed to actually run the suite (41 s).

Where: avail/build.gradle.kts, tasks.test. It passes the roots only as systemProperty("availRoots", availRoots) (computed by computeAvailRootsForTest()), and declares no file inputs for them. The build's other tasks show the pattern for declaring inputs (inputs.files(fileTree(...) { include(...) }), inputs.dir(...)).

Fix: declare the source trees of every root the tests load as test inputs: the .avail files under distro/src (the avail, examples, and builder-tests roots, and any others computeAvailRootsForTest() names), with relative path sensitivity. Exclude the compiled module caches (.repo directories) and anything else the tests write, or every run will invalidate the next.

Check: after the fix, editing one .avail file makes ./gradlew build rerun the tests, and an unchanged tree still lets them be up to date.

title: Implement all Avail file operations through FFM instead of NIO
description:
Goal: implement every Avail file operation directly on the operating system's file interface through the JDK's Foreign Function & Memory API (java.lang.foreign), and stop using NIO (FileChannel, AsynchronousFileChannel, Files) for file I/O. This gives Avail precise control over ordering and durability, so it can host something like a database engine.

Why NIO is inadequate:
- On macOS, FileChannel.force (with either metaData flag) issues fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC) (JDK-8080589, JDK 9; JDK-8232861 refined its failure handling). That flushes the drive's entire write cache: about 16-20 ms per flush, shared by the whole drive. While one is in flight, every metadata-changing call on the volume (create, chmod, unlink) waits for it. A standalone benchmark measured create, chmod, and unlink at about 20.8 ms each beside concurrent F_FULLFSYNC, against under 0.1 ms alone. Plain fsync added about 0.01 ms.
- NIO exposes no weaker sync, no write barrier, no O_DSYNC on every path, and no preallocation, and it hides the file descriptor.

Shape:
- Avail's file handles own native descriptors (POSIX int fd; Windows HANDLE). The calls: open, pread, pwrite, ftruncate, the sync family, fcntl, fstat, fchmod/fchown, rename, unlink, mkdir, readdir, realpath, close. They run on the I/O system's file executor, resuming the calling fiber on completion (see avail-6s8 for the suspendable-primitive shape).
- Sync levels, chosen explicitly by Avail code instead of one fixed meaning:
  - ordering: the writes before the barrier reach media before the writes after it (macOS F_BARRIERFSYNC; elsewhere the nearest equivalent, or the next level up).
  - drive: data and the metadata needed to read it back reach the drive (fsync / fdatasync).
  - durable: also survives power loss (macOS F_FULLFSYNC; on Linux fsync already flushes the drive cache; Windows FlushFileBuffers).
- Errors carry errno (or GetLastError), captured with Linker.Option.captureCallState, and map to AvailErrorCodes.

Cross-platform (the largest part of the cost):
- macOS, Linux, and Windows each need their own bindings, constants, and semantics. Struct layouts (stat), constant values (O_*, F_*), and variadic fcntl differ by platform and architecture (x86_64 and arm64). Windows uses a different API (CreateFileW, ReadFile/WriteFile with OVERLAPPED, FlushFileBuffers, SetFileInformationByHandle).
- jextract can generate the bindings from the system headers, per platform, but it is a build-time tool; decide whether to generate or hand-write the comparatively small set needed.
- The tests must run on each supported platform, or at least on those available to CI.

Notes:
- The JVM flag --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED is already required for a usable look and feel. It is set for packageApp (avail/build.gradle.kts) and in the Avail Project Manager run configuration.
- The test and JUnit launches need the flag as well.
- Kotlin–Avail parity: new error codes, changed failure sets, and the sync levels need library bindings, documentation, and Avail tests.
- Supersedes the idea of a second, FFM-opened descriptor held beside each NIO channel just for fsync, and the question of whether closing a file writer should synchronize; settle both here.
notes: From avail-6s8 (2026-11-10): P_FileRead and P_FileWrite still create a fiber to deliver each result, taking success and failure functions and a priority. Converting them to suspending primitives was deliberately left to this bead, since their NIO paths are replaced here anyway. Every other file primitive already suspends and runs on the I/O system's file executor; follow that shape (suspendThen + runtime.ioSystem.executeFileTask) and remove the library's fiber-returning "a fiber reading…"/"a fiber writing…" file methods, as was done for sync, truncate, rename, and directory creation.

title: Rework fiber-creating file primitives as suspendable primitives
description:
Description:
- Several file primitives, P_FileSync among them, start their work by creating a new fiber. That fiber runs the success or failure function from the I/O system's callback.
- These primitives may predate parts of the suspendable-primitive mechanism.
- Instead, they should suspend the calling fiber and resume it from the I/O system's completion callback, the way reads and writes do. They would no longer create a fiber just to deliver the result.
- Ruling: don't create a fiber merely to handle a suspendable primitive.

Scope:
1. Make P_FileOpen suspendable, running its work on the I/O system's file executor and resuming the fiber from the completion callback. It currently blocks an interpreter thread for the whole open: about 20 ms while a concurrent F_FULLFSYNC is committing, and the workbench profile showed it averaging 19 ms.
2. Do the same for the other synchronous calls that change metadata: P_FileSetPermissions (about 9 ms) and P_FileUnlink (about 4.6 ms). Others, such as P_FileMetadata and rename, are worth checking.
3. Convert the existing fiber-creating primitives, starting with P_FileSync, which currently does newFiber(...) and then runtime.ioSystem.executeFileTask { force(true) … runOutermostFunction(newFiber, …) }. Audit the remaining file and I/O primitives for the same pattern.

Notes:
- The number of these operations in flight at once becomes bounded by the I/O thread pool's size instead of the interpreter threads. That's acceptable: it frees the interpreter threads.
- Evidence:
  - The workbench's L2Simple statistics: P_FileOpen averaged 19.9 ms, P_FileSetPermissions 9.2 ms, and P_FileUnlink 4.6 ms.
  - A standalone benchmark: create, chmod, and unlink each took about 20.8 ms beside concurrent F_FULLFSYNC, against under 0.1 ms alone.
- Primitives whose failure codes or Avail-side bindings change also need their library methods, tests, and documentation updated (Kotlin–Avail parity).
notes:
Landed (2026-11-10, with avail-7i6):
- Every synchronous file primitive that touches the file system now suspends its fiber and runs on the I/O system's file executor: P_FileOpen; the metadata-changing P_FileUnlink, P_FileMove, P_FileCopy, P_FileSetPermissions, P_FileSetOwner, P_FileSetGroup; the read-only P_FileExists, P_FileCanRead, P_FileCanWrite, P_FileCanExecute, P_FileSize, P_FileGetOwner, P_FileGetGroup, P_FileGetPermissions, P_FileMetadata, P_FileRealPath, P_FilesAreSame; and P_FileClose (which now forgets the handle before closing). Their failure codes are unchanged. Primitives that never touch the disk stay synchronous.
- The fiber-creating P_FileSync, P_FileTruncate, P_FileRename, and P_CreateDirectory now suspend instead, without success/failure/priority arguments. Library: Synchronize_with file system and Truncate_to_bytes⁇with file system replace the fiber-returning methods; Rename_to_ and Create a directory named_ call the primitives directly; the fiber-returning variants are removed.
- The socket primitives (P_SocketRead, P_SocketWrite, P_SocketIPv4Connect, P_SocketIPv6Connect, P_ServerSocketAccept) suspend and are resumed by the JVM's completion handler. The fiber-returning network methods are removed; the synchronous methods moved into Client/Primitives.avail and Server/Primitives.avail, and both Synchronous.avail modules were deleted. The network tests fork their own fibers where they need concurrency.
- Primitive.kt: the L2Simple nilpotent-attempt path (L2SimpleTranslator.attemptToEmbedInvocation) now refuses primitives that can suspend or invoke, matching the normal call path (canRunAtSimpleCallSite).

Correction to the description: P_FileRead and P_FileWrite also create fibers; they do not show the suspending shape. Ruling (Mark): their conversion belongs to avail-rlc, where reads and writes are rebuilt on FFM.

Out of scope by ruling: P_ExecuteAttachedExternalProcess creates a fiber attached to the child process's standard streams, which is its purpose, like a fork.

title: Benchmark tracking: catch performance regressions, then guide L2 and translation work
description:
Set up benchmarks whose results are recorded and compared over time.  The
first goal is to catch unnecessary slowdowns of 2x or so before they land.
The second is to measure, and so drive, improvements in L2 execution
speed.  Later, the same setup measures the cost of L2 translation and
optimization itself.

What exists today:
- avail.performance: Statistic, PerInterpreterStatistic, and the
  StatisticReport categories (FINAL_JVM_TRANSLATION_TIME, PRIMITIVES,
  REIFICATIONS, dynamic lookups, type checks, (de)serialization,
  ALLOCATIONS_BY_DESCRIPTOR_CLASS, ...).  These give per-run profiles inside
  the VM, but nothing records them or compares them between runs.
- "Time all tests_times" in Avail Tests.avail prints the wall time of each
  full test pass.  It's crude, but it covers the whole system.
- There is no JMH or kotlinx-benchmark in the build.

Ways to measure:
1. JMH, through the kotlinx-benchmark Gradle plugin or the me.champeau.jmh
   plugin.  This is the standard JVM harness: it handles warm-up, forks,
   statistics, and blackholes, and has profilers for allocation (gc) and
   JIT behavior.  It suits Kotlin-level microbenchmarks such as dispatch,
   type checks, tuple operations, and L2 translation of fixed functions.
   Adding it needs Mark's approval.
2. Benchmarks written in Avail, run by a small Kotlin or JMH harness that
   loads modules once and then times entry points: Avail workloads that run
   through L1, L2, and the JVM-translated chunks.  These are the most
   relevant to L2 work.
3. Counts that don't depend on timing: L2 instructions executed, chunks
   translated, reifications, deoptimizations, and allocations.  These are
   repeatable from run to run, so a change in one is a precise signal even
   on a noisy machine, and the existing Statistic machinery can collect
   them.  A 2x slowdown nearly always shows up as a jump in some count.
4. Compile-time measures: translation and optimization time per function,
   from FINAL_JVM_TRANSLATION_TIME and similar statistics, together with
   the size of each chunk's output (L2 instructions and JVM bytecode).

Ways to track:
- Write each run's results as JSON, keyed by commit, and compare them with
  a saved baseline.  Fail, or warn, when a ratio crosses a threshold such
  as 1.5x for times, or any change at all for counts.  This can be a Gradle
  task, which needs no external service.
- Hosted options exist: Bencher, github-action-benchmark with its GitHub
  Pages charts, and Conbench.  They're optional; local JSON plus a report is
  enough to start, and keeps the data in-house.
- Noise: a 2x threshold tolerates ordinary laptop noise.  Finer goals need
  the same machine, a quiet system, several JMH forks, and medians.

First steps to propose and break down: choose the harness (JMH via a
plugin, or a custom harness); define a small first suite (one or two
fixed-workload Avail entry points plus a few microbenchmarks); add the
deterministic counts; choose the result format and comparison tool.

title: Fix Dokka: kotlinx-html resolution failure in dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml
description:
./gradlew dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml fails in avail (and in
avail-artifact, which it includes) during dependency resolution of the
Dokka HTML generator's runtime classpath:

  Could not resolve all dependencies for configuration
  ':dokkaHtmlGeneratorRuntimeResolver~internal'.
  Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Edge
  org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-html-jvm:0.9.1 (jvmRuntimeElements-published)
  -> org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib-common:1.8.20 has no target nodes.

Gradle surfaces it as "Problems writing to Binary store in
~/.gradle/.tmp/gradle*.bin", and with the configuration cache on, as a
cache serialization error; --no-configuration-cache shows the same root
cause.  It is the same error that kept gradle-plugin on Dokka 2.1.0 during
the Gradle 9.8.2 / Kotlin 2.4.21 upgrade (commit 8a4d05e18), which likely
introduced it.  Suspects: kotlin-stdlib-common no longer being published
for Kotlin 2.4 (no matching variant), a dependency-resolution or
substitution rule in the build, or a Dokka version mismatch with Gradle 9.8.

Dokka is the KDoc link checker named in CLAUDE.md's "Verifying a Change",
so until it is fixed new KDoc links go unchecked.  Done when
dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml succeeds in avail (and gradle-plugin can move
to the same Dokka version), with the configuration cache on.

title: Navigate from IntelliJ stack frames to dumped L2 classes and .l2 files
description:
When debugging a live VM in IntelliJ, stack frames in generated JVMChunk
classes cannot be navigated: neither to the dumped .class file nor, ideally,
to the .l2 text, whose line numbers the class's LineNumberTable already
records.  Making this work would let a JVM debugger step through L2 code.

What exists (optimizer/jvm/JVMTranslator.kt, with debugJVM enabled):
- Each chunk's .class is dumped under debug/jvm/<package path>/ (relative
  to the process working directory, so avail/debug/jvm when run from
  avail/), beside its .l1, .l2, .dot, and .simple.dot files.
- The class records SourceFile as the .l2 file name, e.g. "0000
  group_by_#1.l2", and its line numbers refer to lines of that .l2 file.
- Class names are derived from module and method names, e.g.
  avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.Maps.0000_group_by_#1 (2).group_by_#1.
  The package segments contain spaces, parentheses, '#', and characters
  such as '«', which are not Java identifiers.

Likely causes to investigate:
- The debugger resolves a frame's source as <package dirs>/<SourceFile>
  under a source root; debug/jvm is not a source root, and the .l2 file
  is not where that lookup would place it, or IntelliJ cannot map the
  non-identifier package names to directories at all.
- The class files are not on any classpath IntelliJ knows about.

Possible directions: sanitize generated package and class names to valid
identifiers (keeping a readable mapping), lay out the dump so that
<package dirs>/<SourceFile> names the .l2 file exactly, and register
debug/jvm as a source root (or document how to attach it) so the .l2 file
opens at the frame's line.
notes:
Findings (2026-11-06, verified by Mark in IntelliJ):
- Generated classes now use Java-identifier names:
  avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.<Module>.L<line>_<function>_v<n>.<function>,
  dumped under avail/debug/jvm mirroring the package
  (JVMTranslator.prepareOutputDirectory).
- IntelliJ's Java debugger finds a frame's source by looking up a Java file
  that declares the class, through its index, within the run configuration's
  module scope.  A plain .l2 file declares nothing, so it is never found.
  Hence JVMTranslator.dumpL2ListingAsJava = true: the listing is written as
  <function>.java, declaring the class, with the listing in a comment on
  unchanged lines.
- avail/.idea/misc.xml had the project compiler output set to
  $PROJECT_DIR$/debug/jvm, and IntelliJ never indexes the project output
  directory.  Changed to $PROJECT_DIR$/out (misc.xml is untracked).
- IntelliJ setup that works: avail/debug/jvm as a content root of module
  avail.main, marked Sources, and listed under Settings > Compiler >
  Excludes (the project builds with IntelliJ's own compiler,
  delegatedBuild = false, so the stubs must not be compiled).  A Gradle
  re-sync may drop the content root.
- Register names (r0, i1, ...) come from the class's LocalVariableTable,
  now emitted whenever debugJVM is on; locals are not initialized, so a
  register not yet written shows no meaningful value.
Remaining option if the .java form is unwanted: an IntelliJ plugin with a
PositionManagerFactory mapping avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.* frames to
debug/jvm/<sourcePath>, which would make plain .l2 work.
Preferred solution (Mark, 2026-11-06): Kotlin listings with the original
class names.  JVMTranslator.l2ListingFormat = L2ListingFormat.KOTLIN and
useOriginalClassNames = true.  Each generated class lives in package
avail.optimizer.jvm.generated.<module>.<line>_<function> (<n>) and its
listing is <function>.kt, declaring the class with every name segment in
backticks and the listing inside a block comment (both /* and */ broken
apart, since Kotlin comments nest).  Verified in IntelliJ: double-clicking
a generated frame opens the .kt listing at the right L2 instruction, and
register locals (r0, i1, ...) show by name.  kotlinc 2.4.21 compiles these
listings to classes with exactly the generated names; '%' only draws a
Windows warning.

The JAVA format (with Java-identifier names, useOriginalClassNames = false)
and the plain TEXT format (.l2, not navigable) remain selectable.

IntelliJ setup that navigation needs: debug/jvm is a content root of module
avail.main marked Sources, listed under Compiler > Excludes, and the project
output (misc.xml) is NOT debug/jvm (it was, which stopped indexing).

title: Autocompletion in the Avail module editor
description:
Offer completions while typing in an Avail module editor (anvil/AvailEditor.kt,
anvil/text/CodePane.kt).  Use the parsing state at the caret, via
ParsingPlanInProgressDescriptor (descriptor/parsing/), to determine what can
come next: the tokens that would advance an in-progress message plan, and the
in-scope variables whose types fit an argument position the plan expects.

No completion support exists in anvil/ yet.

title: Complete the Avail debugger
description:
Finish the Anvil debugger (avail/src/main/kotlin/avail/anvil/debugger/
AvailDebugger.kt).

Unwired actions: stepOutAction ("Out", shift-F8), stepToLineAction
("To Line"), and restartAction ("Restart") are disabled and only show a
"not implemented" dialog.

Layout: the debugger's panes have no resize bars.  AvailWorkbench uses
JSplitPane for this; the debugger should do the same.

Smaller gaps: two TODOs in AvailDebugger.kt about preserving the variable
selection when the selected frame changes.

title: L2 function inlining
description:
Inline called functions into the caller's L2 control flow graph.

Context for breaking it down: Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 9.2 notes
that L2ValueManifest.transform (currently without callers) is intended for
inlining called graphs, where the callee's stack slots must be distinguished
from the caller's via Frame, and that post-phi data keyed by semantic values
must be transformed along with it.  Survey what inlining the optimizer already
does before proposing children.

title: Remove what post-phi data makes unnecessary; add the never-used exclusion pass
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 8 lists mechanisms the post-phi data makes
unnecessary, and a never-used exclusion pass it makes possible.  Remove the
former and add the latter, once the invariants of the sibling beads are
asserted.

title: Postpone, rather than drop, inputs read only by postponed instructions
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 5 (closing note) and 10.4: an input that
is read only by a postponed instruction must itself be postponed rather than
dropped.  Check whether this holds today; fix it if not.  The failure it
causes resembles the ones the post-phi design exists to end.

title: Assert each output edge is at least as informative as its input edge
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md sections 6 and 10.3: after regeneration and
post-phi replay, each output edge's manifest must be at least as informative
as the corresponding input edge's (the monotonicity law).  Add a per-edge
assertion.  Verify against testSemanticRestrictionOfSetCreation_1.

title: Assert the witness invariant on each post-phi capture
description:
Declared_Manifest_Effects.md section 5: every synonym captured in post-phi
data must have a witness, namely a register holding it, a constant
restriction, or a self-describing member.  Assert this at capture time.  It is
the property the design turns on, and it would catch a value whose only
witness was a postponement.

title: Finish the declared-manifest-effects design
description:
The post-phi data mechanism (L2BasicBlock.postPhiData) is captured, replayed,
and rendered, but the remaining items of the design in
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Declared_Manifest_Effects.md (its "Suggested
order", items 2, 3, 4, and 5) were not found in the code.  Read that doc
(sections 4-8) first.

title: Bring Variable_elision.md in line with the implementation
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Variable_elision.md says "This is not exactly
what was implemented", and its "Reworked form (proposed ~Oct 12, 2024)" section
describes L2_VIRTUAL_GET_VARIABLE / L2_VIRTUAL_SET_VARIABLE, which do not exist.
Rewrite it to describe the variable elision the optimizer actually performs.
The reworked design, if still wanted, is tracked by its own bead.

title: Delete Configuration_Cache_Fixes_Needed.md
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/Configuration_Cache_Fixes_Needed.md lists Gradle
configuration-cache fixes for avail/build.gradle.kts.  They have landed: the
incompatible project.extensions / rootProject.projectDir patterns are gone and
org.gradle.configuration-cache=true is set in avail/gradle.properties.  Confirm,
then delete the file (ask Mark before deleting).

title: Make the Focus Filter docs normative; delete the integration plan
description:
FocusFilter and NoFilter (L2ControlFlowGraphVisualizationFilter.kt) are
implemented and wired into L2ControlFlowGraphVisualizer.  Turn
avail/doc/Optimization/Focus_Filter_Design_Summary.md into a description of the
filter as built (or fold it into the KDoc of
L2ControlFlowGraphVisualizationFilter, whichever reads better), and delete
avail/doc/Optimization/Focus_Filter_Integration_Plan.md, which is an executed
plan (ask Mark before deleting).  Remaining follow-ups are tracked separately.

title: Fold manifest invariants into L2ValueManifest KDoc; retire the session notes
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/TODO_Documentation_Updates.md and
avail/doc/Optimization/Debugging_Session_2025-01-26.md are session notes, not
design.  Move their lasting content into KDoc on L2ValueManifest (and its
neighbors) where it is still true of the current code:
- populated versus postponed semantic values, and the invariant tying a value
  with no definitions to its postponed instruction;
- hasSemanticValue versus hasLiveSemanticValue, equivalentSemanticValue
  versus equivalentPopulatedSemanticValue;
- SSA uniqueness applies to registers, not semantic values (merge points
  create several registers for one value).
Check each claim against the code (the manifest was redesigned since 2025).
Then delete both note files (ask Mark before deleting).

title: Make avail/doc/Optimization normative
description:
Bring every document under avail/doc/Optimization in line with the rule that

title: Hoist loop-body type tests by unrolling one iteration
description: Use the result of an earlier loop generation pass to decide whether to build a variation without an inner type test that always holds (or never holds), hoisting the test out of the loop by unrolling one iteration.

title: Int-register conditions at loop heads
description: Specialize loop variations that keep values in int registers across the loop.

title: Drop duplicate loop variations
description: Compare a newly generated loop variation's instructions with earlier ones, and reuse a match instead of keeping a copy.

title: Generate loop-head variations and link backward branches
description: Build a loop head and body specialized for a set of conditions, and connect each backward branch to the most specific variation that satisfies it.

title: Propagate split conditions backward to loop heads
description: Carry the L2SplitConditions requested inside a loop body back along its backward branches to the loop head, so the head can be split on them.

title: Loop splitting
description:
Extend L2 code splitting to loop heads.  A loop head is split into
variations specialized for the L2SplitConditions propagated backward to it
(see avail/src/main/kotlin/avail/optimizer/L2SplitCondition.kt), and each
backward branch that closes a loop connects to the most specific available
variation of the loop head.

When a backward branch from a generated body requests conditions that no
existing variation satisfies, generate a new variation, then compare its
instructions against the previously generated variations; if it is
equivalent to one of them, reuse that one and discard the duplicate.

Kinds of condition:
- A value must be in an int register.
- A type condition tested inside the body holds (or never holds).

For a type test inside the body, use the result of a previous loop
generation pass to decide whether to create a variation without the test.
Doing so hoists the test out of the loop by unrolling one iteration.

title: Update copyright years to 2026 in Kotlin, Avail, and Java sources
description:
Bring every Avail Foundation copyright notice up to the current year:
"Copyright © 1993-2026, The Avail Foundation, LLC."  This covers the Kotlin
sources (.kt, and the .kts build scripts that carry the header), the Avail
modules (.avail), and the handful of Java files.

Survey of tracked files (2026-11-07):
- .kt (1639 files): 1362 say 1993-2022, 20 say 1993-2019, 59 say 1993-2023,
  50 say 1993-2024, 5 say 1993-2025, and 103 already say 1993-2026.  40 have
  no notice.
- .kts (16 files): 7 say 1993-2022; one says "1993-" with no end year
  (likely a template variable that never expanded); 9 have no notice.
- .avail (819 files): 798 say 1993-2022, 2 say 1993-2019, 4 say 1993-2023,
  1 says 1993-2024, and 7 already say 1993-2026.  5 say "2013-2015" and 1
  says "2019,": check whose notices these are before touching them; they may
  belong to someone else (examples, or imported code).  1 has no notice.
- .java (9 files): 7 say 1993-2022; 2 have no notice.

Only the end year of the "1993-YYYY" range changes.  The rest of each
header stays exactly as it is.  Files with no notice, and notices that
aren't the Foundation's 1993 range, are listed for Mark to decide.  They
aren't changed silently.  The IntelliJ file template
(avail/.idea/fileTemplates/includes/File Header.java) presumably computes
the year already; confirm it does.

A bulk mechanical edit is the exception to the "Edit tool, not scripts" rule
for this one change.  Show Mark the exact command and a sample diff first.
Watch out: paths contain spaces, so use NUL-separated lists (git ls-files -z
| xargs -0).

Every Avail module's text changes, so the .repo compiled caches are rebuilt
on the next load and the next full build is slow.  Done when the build and
tests pass, and no Foundation notice in these file types has an end year
other than 2026.

title: Avail test runner underuses concurrent fibers (200-300% CPU on 12 cores)
description:
Running all the Avail-language tests repeatedly keeps only 2-3 cores busy,
at 200-300% CPU, on a 12-core machine.  This happens with "Run all tests
repeatedly" or "Time all tests_times" in Avail Tests.avail.  The Avail
unit-testing framework forks fibers to run tests concurrently, but far
fewer run at once than Mark expects.  Find out why, and fix it.  (JUnit's
own parallelism, the Gradle side, is a separate matter.)

How the runner schedules tests today (Avail.avail/Unit Testing.avail/
Runners.avail, "recursively report on all tests in_"):
- "recursively visit_,on entering do_,on leaving do_" walks the suite tree
  depth first, one suite at a time, using For each over child suite IDs.
- Within one suite, the tests that have no per-test fixtures run with
  "map parallel in parallel through computeMetric".  The tests that do have
  fixtures, and every test in a suite marked "Do not run tests in_in
  parallel" (file iterator and file access rights tests, for example), then
  run one at a time.
- So concurrency is limited to one suite's parallel tests at a time.  Each
  suite waits for its slowest test, and its serial tests, before the next
  suite starts.  Small suites, or suites with one long test, leave the cores
  idle.  This is the leading hypothesis, but it is not yet measured.

Questions to answer:
- Measure it: how many fibers are runnable over time, and how busy the
  AvailRuntime pool's workers are.  The pool size depends on the processor
  count.  A JFR recording, thread dumps, or fiber counts taken during a
  loop would show this.
- How is "map_in parallel through_" implemented (one fiber per element, or
  bounded)?  Does it add overhead or a limit of its own?
- Apart from the suite structure, do the tests serialize on something else:
  shared variables or locks in the framework (Framework State.avail), the
  L2 optimizer or JVM translation (chunk compilation, nameCounters), or
  output to standard out?
- Would running whole suites concurrently, honoring fixture and
  "do not run in parallel" constraints, raise utilization?  Suite fixture
  setup and teardown must still bracket each suite's tests.

Done when the bottleneck is identified with evidence, and the runner's
scheduling (or whatever else limits it) is changed, so that a full test run
keeps the cores busy, or the limit is explained.
notes: Ruling (Mark, 2026-11-07): a child suite's tests follow the per-test fixture rules they inherit.  So a suite that declares its own per-test fixture (Before running each test in_, or Do not run tests in_in parallel) runs its whole subtree in one sequential chain, as the runner does today.  Child suites' suite-level setup and teardown still bracket their own tests within that chain.  Elsewhere the scheme is concurrent: a suite's setup runs first; then its fixture-free tests, each of its child suites, and its chain of tests that must run one at a time all run concurrently; then its teardown.  Unwrap worker exceptions so that test-fixture-setup and test-fixture-tear-down exceptions keep their types.  Measure CPU use and wall time with Time all tests_times before and after.

title: Rework variable elision around virtual get/set instructions
description:
The "Reworked form (proposed ~Oct 12, 2024)" of

title: L2_INVOKE_WITH_OUTERS: call closed code without building the closure
description:
avail/doc/Optimization/Level_Two/Function_call_with_outers.md: the pattern
r1 = L2_CLOSE(code, outers...); L2_INVOKE(r1, args...) is common.  Replace it
with L2_INVOKE_WITH_OUTERS(code, [outers], [args]), passing outers and
arguments together on an interpreter-held argument stack (extending
argsBuffer), callee-pops (or caller-pops, to allow combining pops), cleared on
reification.  A plain L2_INVOKE of a passed-in function pushes the outers of
that function itself.

title: Variant consistency between manifest and restrictions
description:
Step 8 of the manifest redesign (Manifest_ValueClass_Redesign.md): keep the
variant sets in TypeRestriction (they are read where no manifest exists:
L2_GET_OBJECT_FIELD.translateToJVM, L2_GET_OBJECT_TYPE_FIELD,
L2_EXTRACT_OBJECT_VARIANT_ID, and the dispatch lookup trees).  Make the
manifest the sole writer of variant information into restrictions, reconcile
the two at every update, and have L2ValueManifest.check() assert consistency.
No such assertion exists today.

title: Constants as a ValueState field (constantOf)
description:
Step 7 of the manifest redesign (Manifest_ValueClass_Redesign.md): add
constantOf on the value state and remove the L2SemanticConstant special cases
from the manifest's equivalence test (avail/src/main/kotlin/avail/optimizer/
manifest/L2ValueManifest.kt, around the "otherSemanticValue is
L2SemanticConstant" cases near line 2156).  Keep L2SemanticConstant as the
canonical member; do not delete the class.

title: E-graph saturation for primitive-invocation equivalences
description:
Listed as out of scope in Manifest_ValueClass_Redesign.md: equivalences of
L2SemanticPrimitiveInvocation driven by declared theorems with a cost model
